description: Knowledge base assessment from interview notes or five questions. Maps where business knowledge lives, scores value and readiness, plans the first build. Returns content only.

input.description: Knowledge base assessment request: interview notes, a transcript or answers to KB 1-5 about what knowledge the business needs and where it lives, the business description and speaker labels, in the respondent's words. Send only information needed for this assessment; omit sensitive personal identifiers and file contents. STATIC HOST METADATA host_review: Unreviewed draft. Before rendering, compare every area, score, source, owner, step and claim with the current source and correct anything unsupported; unknowns say To confirm. Delete any area, source, owner or question the source does not name. Recheck each score on its scale (value: how often the knowledge is needed and what goes wrong without it, never lowered because capture is hard; readiness: 1 only in someone's head, 3 scattered files or a manual export, 5 written down and current in a tool the client uses) and each quadrant (high is 4 or 5: populate_now high value and high readiness, capture_first high value with readiness 3 or less, fill_in value 3 or less with high readiness, defer both 3 or less, unscored when either score is Unknown). first_build is one area from areas: the highest-value populate_now area whenever one exists, else the highest-value capture_first area, else the area the client most needs. test_question is a question the source says customers or the team ask, in its words. A tool that offers a connector is not a connection: never say a source is connected, and check any connector claim on the vendor's official page before it reaches the deck. Exactly 4 plan steps, each naming one who: Owner or one role the source names, never another and never two roles joined by or; exactly 2 next steps. Delete any later item the source gives no need for. Keep IDs, quotes, evidence and numeric scores off the slides. Ask the user for the client's logo; never invent one. Render with the pinned branding and the knowledge base deck layout; verify asset hashes and inspect every slide. If an asset is unavailable, follow the fallback rule and disclose it. Claim only files actually created. Disclose corrections separately from the deck. (1) Cover: centred vertically, KNOWLEDGE BASE in #FFFFFF over ASSESSMENT in #F06000, Montserrat 800 132px uppercase, line height .9; 30px below, Prepared for and the client, or the business type when the client is Unknown (#FFFFFF, 600), in Inter 34px #F0E0D0. Pinned to the bottom of the safe area, a full-width row with a 1px rule top border and 30px top padding: three columns packed to the left, each only as wide as its text and 84px apart: keys Assessment Date (today, written out, such as November 12, 2026), Business Type and Primary Focus in mono 24px, values 10px below in Inter 27px #FFFFFF. The client's logo sits top right inside the safe area, 120px high on a #FFFFFF panel with 14px padding, only when the user attached it (ask once; never fetch, redraw or invent it). (2) Executive Summary, eyebrow Where we are · where we’re going: a 1.25fr and 1fr grid with 32px gaps filling the slide. Left: two stacked equal cards, The Pain and The Outcome, each a Montserrat 800 30px uppercase #F06000 heading (letter spacing .16em) 18px above Inter 27px/1.5 #F0E0D0 text, centred vertically. (3) Value–Readiness Map, eyebrow Where the value is: a 56px axis column beside a 2x2 grid of quadrant cards with 20px gaps, a 52px axis row below, 18px between. Each area in its quadrant as a tag, 10px apart, in Inter 600 22px with padding 8px 14px: #000000 on rgba(0,0,0,.18) in Populate Now, #FFFFFF on #242424 elsewhere. Unscored areas go on one mono line under the grid, such as Not yet scored · Warranty terms. Drop this slide when no area is scored. (4) Where Your Knowledge Lives, eyebrow The sources: a header row in mono 20px #8090A0 (Source, What it holds, Owner, Status), then one row per source with 20px top and bottom padding and a 1px rule above each row and below the last, in columns 64px, 1fr, 1.4fr, .8fr and 220px with 28px gaps: the number 01 in Montserrat 800 34px #F06000, the name in Inter 600 27px #FFFFFF, holds and owner in Inter 24px #F0E0D0, and the status as a tag in Montserrat 800 20px uppercase (letter spacing .08em, padding 8px 14px): Ready #000000 on #F06000, Export and Capture #FFFFFF on #242424, To confirm #8090A0 with a 1px rule2 border. (5) Your 4-Step Build Plan, eyebrow Build the first area, on #1A1A1A: four equal columns with 26px gaps filling the slide; each card #1A1A1A with a 1px rule border and padding 34px 32px: the number 1 to 4 in Montserrat 800 88px, line height .9, #F06000; Step One to Step Four 10px below in Montserrat 800 26px uppercase #FFFFFF (letter spacing .14em); the task 22px below in Inter 27px/1.45 #F0E0D0; at the bottom, over a 1px rule with 22px padding, one uppercase line: WHO · in mono 24px #8090A0 (letter spacing .1em) and, on the same line, who in Montserrat 800 uppercase #F06000. (6) What It Unlocks, eyebrow The next phase: three top-aligned columns 32px apart, no cards, the row centred vertically, one per later item (the remaining columns stay empty): the number 01 in Montserrat 800 96px, line height .85, #F06000; a 60x2px rule2 line with 26px above and below; text in Inter 500 42px/1.25 #FFFFFF; name 18px below in mono 24px (letter spacing .1em). Drop this slide without a later item. (7) Your Next Steps, eyebrow Let’s get moving, on #1A1A1A: the two steps centred vertically, 30px apart, at most 1320px wide: the number in Montserrat 800 80px #F06000 in a 96px column, 34px gap; heading in Montserrat 800 42px uppercase #FFFFFF (letter spacing .02em); detail 12px below in Inter 27px/1.45 #F0E0D0, at most 980px wide; 14px under step 2, the button Schedule Your Review Call → on #F06000 in Montserrat 800 28px uppercase #000000 (letter spacing .08em), padding 24px 40px. Number the slides in order (01 / 06 when one is dropped). Character limits are maxima, not targets; shorten copy rather than shrinking type or clipping. Use Montserrat, Inter and the authentic logo only after verifying the supplied asset hashes; never redraw, recolor or replace the logo. Never deliver unbranded files silently. Deliver the deck PDF and the same deck as standalone HTML with both fonts embedded. areas.description: 1-8 areas, only those the source names.

name.description: A kind of knowledge the source names, in the client's words; never one the source does not name. At most 24 characters.

quadrant.description: From the two scores; unscored when either is Unknown.

business_type.description: Such as Home services company. At most 40 characters.

client.description: The client's name only if the source states it, else Unknown. At most 60 characters.

first_build.description: The name of one area from areas: the highest-value populate_now area whenever one exists, else the highest-value capture_first area, else the area the client most needs. At most 24 characters.

focus.description: The primary focus, such as Pricing and job history. At most 40 characters.

text.description: What the knowledge base makes possible next. At most 70 characters.

next_steps.description: Exactly 2: start Step 1 this week; what to note for the review call.

outcome.description: What changes once the first area is built, and what the owner still does. At most 200 characters.

pain.description: One or two sentences in the client's terms. At most 200 characters.

task.description: A plain action naming who does it. At most 130 characters.

sources.description: 1-8 sources, only those the source names.

holds.description: What it holds. At most 60 characters.

name.description: A tool, file store, inbox or person named in the source. At most 30 characters.

owner.description: The role the source says keeps it current, else To confirm. At most 30 characters.

status.description: Ready (a spreadsheet or app kept current), Export (documents, PDFs or files to gather), Capture (only in someone's head) or To confirm.

test_question.description: A question the source says customers or the team ask, in its words, that the first build must answer with a current source. At most 120 characters.
